explanation: In the Republic, chained prisoners see only shadows cast by a fire. One is freed, climbs into the sunlight and learns what things really are. The same book compares a state to a ship.

claims.text: In Plato's allegory of the cave, prisoners inside a cave take shadows on the wall for reality.
Plato's allegory of the shadows is not set on a ship, in a temple or in a forest.
The allegory of the cave appears in Plato's Republic.
In the allegory, chained prisoners see only shadows cast by a fire, and a freed prisoner climbs out into the sunlight.
Plato's Republic also compares a state to a ship, in the image known as the ship of state.
